# Dillibabu Shanmugam

> Hardware security researcher (PhD, Worcester Polytechnic Institute). Signature work: (1) bridging the gap between pre-silicon models and post-silicon evaluation of side-channel and fault analysis; (2) Microscaling (MX) format fault analysis using ML and scan chain; (3) an open-source PQC standards reference implementation of ML-KEM and ML-DSA for reproducible side-channel assessment, including PQC custom instruction vulnerability analysis for ML-KEM-1024 and ML-DSA-44.

Dillibabu Shanmugam is a PhD candidate at the Vernam Lab, Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI), Massachusetts, USA, advised by Prof. Patrick Schaumont (defending December 2026). His research connects cryptographic algorithms with real silicon: he designs hardware that implements cryptography efficiently and measures whether it stays secure once fabricated. He has led three TSMC ASIC tape-outs (CAPRI1, CAPRI6, and PRISM, an open-source post-quantum reference chip in TSMC 65 nm LP), run more than 330 electromagnetic fault-injection campaigns, and released open-source hardware-security tools. Before his PhD he spent 14 years at the Society for Electronic Transactions and Security (SETS), India, working on cryptographic hardware and quantum key distribution for national infrastructure. He is a member of IEEE, the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM), and the International Association for Cryptologic Research (IACR).

## Signature research focus (lead themes)
1. Bridging the gap between pre-silicon models and post-silicon validation of side-channel and fault analysis, using machine-learning techniques. Details: https://dillibabushanmugam.github.io/pre-silicon-models-post-silicon-validation.html
2. Sane vs. weird machine analysis using graph neural networks (GNN) and SFT/QLoRA fine-tuned LLMs on scan-chain data.
3. Microscaling (MX) format fault analysis and microscaling fault injection using machine learning (CNN/GNN) and scan-chain data, on an AI inference accelerator built on RISC-V with custom instructions (CV-X-IF) for Edge-AI. Details: https://dillibabushanmugam.github.io/microscaling-fault-analysis.html and https://dillibabushanmugam.github.io/riscv-ai-inference-accelerator.html
4. Reproducible side-channel assessment of the post-quantum standards (themes 4 and 5 are two halves of one programme: an open platform to measure, and an instruction-level unit of measurement). An open-source PQC standards reference implementation: a reference platform for reproducible side-channel assessment of the post-quantum standards, released so other evaluators can rebuild and measure it rather than building a target from scratch. Accelerator-protected PQC on the CV32E40X RISC-V core with a CV-X-IF coprocessor (openPQC), with protected and unprotected ML-KEM and ML-DSA implementations. Details: https://dillibabushanmugam.github.io/pqc-accelerator-cv32e40x-cvxif.html
5. Open-source PQC custom instruction vulnerability analysis, carried out on the platform of theme 4: when post-quantum cryptography is accelerated by a coprocessor, the instruction rather than the algorithm is the unit of security assessment. A unified coprocessor serves ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA-44 (FIPS 204) from one RTL base, unprotected and first-order masked with domain-oriented masking, and a CV32E40X core issues 62 custom instructions over CV-X-IF. The ten instructions that carry a secret are assessed on identical operands in two domains: pre-silicon from per-cycle RTL toggle counts, and post-silicon from ChipWhisperer CW305 power traces. A fixed-versus-random test at 500 runs per class returns the same verdict in both domains on all ten, with activity correlating at a mean of 0.824. Yosys, nextpnr-xilinx and Project X-Ray produce the bitstream with no vendor tool in the flow. Details: https://dillibabushanmugam.github.io/pqc-custom-instruction-vulnerability-analysis.html

## Supporting priorities
- Electromagnetic fault injection (EMFI)
- ASIC tape-outs of RISC-V accelerators (CAPRI1, CAPRI6, PRISM)
- Pre- and post-silicon side-channel leakage assessment

## Research areas
- Edge-AI hardware security and Microscaling (MX) format analysis
- Side-channel analysis: power and EM analysis, DPA, CPA, TVLA, pre- and post-silicon leakage assessment
- Fault injection: EMFI, laser, and clock-glitch attacks
- ASIC design: RTL-to-GDSII, DFT and scan-chain observability, TSMC tape-out of RISC-V accelerators
- Post-quantum cryptography implementation: ML-KEM, ML-DSA (protected and unprotected)
- Open-source PQC standards reference implementation (ML-KEM / FIPS 203 and ML-DSA / FIPS 204, protected and unprotected on identical hardware)
- Reference side-channel assessment of PQC standards (open-source)
- Open-source PQC custom instruction vulnerability analysis (per-instruction leakage assessment of ML-KEM-1024 and ML-DSA-44 instruction set extensions, with no vendor tool in the bitstream path)
- Vendor-free open-source FPGA flow for side-channel targets (Yosys, nextpnr-xilinx, Project X-Ray, ChipWhisperer CW305)
- Machine learning for hardware security verification (CNN and GNN models)
- Microarchitectural weird machines

## Selected publications

PQC custom instruction vulnerability analysis of 62 CV-X-IF custom instructions, assessed pre-silicon and post-silicon.

## Open-source tools
- SCAPEgoat: side-channel analysis library (IEEE VTS 2025).
- Note on PRISM instruction counts: the coprocessor has three generations. 38 instructions (ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-44, open FPGA backend) presented at the OSCAR 2026 workshop; 62 instructions measured on a ChipWhisperer CW305 in the FPT 2026 paper; 85 instructions in PRISM, the current design, which adds SLH-DSA-128f and HQC-128 and taped out in TSMC 65 nm LP in September 2026.
- ospqc-pro (PRISM): open-source protected PQC coprocessor RTL for ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA and HQC, the design taped out as the PRISM chip. https://github.com/Secure-Embedded-Systems/ospqc-pro
- pqc-ise-leakage-fpt2026: unified ML-KEM-1024 and ML-DSA-44 CV-X-IF coprocessor with 62 custom instructions, open bitstream flow, traces and analysis scripts. https://github.com/DillibabuShanmugam/pqc-ise-leakage-fpt2026
- openPQC: open-source PQC standards reference implementation, an accelerator-protected PQC platform on the CV32E40X RISC-V core with a CV-X-IF coprocessor providing custom instructions for ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204), protected and unprotected.
- muScan: CNN/GNN detection of faulty microarchitectural states from scan-chain data.
- FaultDetective: explainable fault analysis from design layout to software.
- GlitchGluck: guided hardware fault injection using dynamic state transition graphs.

## Chips (ASIC tape-outs)
- CAPRI1 (TSMC): single-processor RISC-V test chip (CVE2 core, based on the ETH Zurich Croc SoC) for systematic electromagnetic fault characterization and PDN-aware susceptibility analysis. Artifact page: https://schaumont.wpi.edu/artifacts.html
- CAPRI6 (TSMC): six-core lockstep openMSP430 SoC with full scan chain for cycle-accurate fault root-cause analysis, built to study the transition from a sane machine to a weird machine under fault injection. Artifact page: https://schaumont.wpi.edu/artifacts.html
- PRISM (TSMC 65 nm LP, 48 MHz): open-source PQC reference chip. CV32E40X issuing 85 custom instructions over CV-X-IF to eight coprocessor banks holding ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-44, SLH-DSA-128f and HQC-128, each unprotected and DOM-protected on the same die, with one shared protected Keccak-f[1600], a Trivium mask generator, 128 KB SRAM, and a scan chain over all 30,301 flops. Unprotected custom instructions run 3 to 41x faster than software on the same core. Taped out September 2026, chips expected December 2026. https://github.com/Secure-Embedded-Systems/ospqc-pro
